private_note: Alder keeps the same expected income as Today (100) but lifts my floor from 22 to 32 and guarantees health coverage, so it beats Today outright. Cedar's higher average (115) isn't worth a 1-in-5 chance of 15 with no coverage. Hazel and Birch give up too much average. Today goes last: a failed convention leaves me exposed at the bottom with no coverage, and Alder is the realistic plan most delegates can reach 9 votes on.
statement: Fellow delegates, we each face the same lottery: a one-in-five chance of every group. Look at Alder. Its average household income is 100, exactly the same as today, yet the lowest fifth rises from 22 to 32 and every household is guaranteed basic health coverage. Compared with today, Alder costs us nothing on average and protects each of us against the worst draw. Cedar offers a higher average, but one of us in five lands at 15 with no health coverage, for a generation. Hazel and Birch protect the bottom but cut the average by a fifth or more, which we all pay in four draws out of five. Alder is the balanced choice: insurance without sacrificing prosperity. Remember too that we need nine of twelve. If we split, the convention fails and we keep today's arrangements, which are worse than Alder for every self-interested delegate. I urge you to rank Alder first.
